content:
Hi, I opened four PRs about bluebell in iris-lean https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean/issues?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+author%3Apirapira but hasn't got feedbacks.

If there are not enough reviewers on this repo, I think I can help with reviews too.
Ah, sorry I'd only seen the one I merged when I looked last week (downside of reviewing PRs in a cab). I'm back home now, so I'll get to these today.

Great. Most PRs are straightforward.

wp_frame needed an assumption CMRA.IsTotal (IndexedPSpPm I α V F). https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean/pull/242/files#diff-98c4f9e17c1ab867fa300750c35aab05e0ac71a01714e74a986642bf1805f3d2R59

This made me wonder we might want to use a UCMRA (esp with zero permission allowed), so I opened an issue https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean/issues/243

CMRA.IsTotal (IndexedPSpPm I α V F) is assumed in a few places but it is false.

I think we need to replace it with a UCMRA (esp. with permissions being non-negative rational numbers).

I filed an issue https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean/issues/248 for CMRA.IsTotal (IndexedPSpPm I α V F) being false. Can I replace the CMRA with a UCMRA (by changing the permission to PermissionRat)? @Quang Dao

Is there a detailed roadmap for "bleubell in iris"? Does this just mean using the proof mode, or is there an ambition to do a full encoding. Because the bluebell paper does not seem to document how to do that (yet?).
My personal plan has been to try a full encoding till I'm stuck and then to call one of the iris people. I think I need the unit for the pure modality so a UCMRA would be useful.

We went over the Bluebell paper in a seminar here in Aarhus (one of the iris centers). The iris experts here where somewhat skeptical that a full encoding would be straight-forward.
I'd be happy to put you in contact with them.
Yes, I'd love to hear what they think, especially since they are seeing some difficulties I haven't perceived yet.
Is there a plan to upstream the work in https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean to the main branch at some point in the future?

@Yoichi Hirai My recollection from the seminar: encoding bluebell in iris might work for a semantics with only finite distributions, no concurrency, no while loops (just for-loops), adding state might already be hard
I believe iris-lean currently has no programming language (e.g. heaplang) yet, does it?

Is there a formalization of the semantics of Bluebell (or lilac for that matter?).

Janine Lohse (MPI) is working on adding the "conditional" modality to rocq-iris, so if you want to go in that direction, it might be good to reach out.

upstream

Not that I know but why not. Do you know @Alexander Hicks

I think we can ask this again when the fork becomes in decent shape.

encoding bluebell in iris might work for a semantics with only finite distributions, no concurrency, no while loops (just for-loops), adding state might already be hard

Now I see. I feel these are still far away. Getting finite distribution and finite loop right is already interesting for understanding and testing main ideas of bluebell. I still don't know which features matter more. The advantage of doing this kind of thing here is that we can easily find increasingly demanding examples.

Here's the work that has been scoped out so far (rouhgly summarising high level milestones from the grant).
(i) embedding Bluebell into Iris-Lean
(ii) integration with the VCV-io, including
(iii) This should make it possible to model the heap and state of most of the languages that we
intend to target.
(iv) Creation of an extraction pipeline from a subset of the Iris iProp type into the
non-linear integer arithmetic theory of SMT-LIB. (I guess there's some dependency there on general Lean<>SMT work as well the improved support for non linear integer arithmetic that's on the Lean FRO roadmap.)
(v) A proof-of-concept verification effort targeting e.g. multi-instance extractability of Merkle Trees as outlined in the SNARGS book.

Is there a plan to upstream the work in https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean to the main branch at some point in the future?

This depends on iris-lean being ok with the mathlib dependency which require, which they are not (hence our fork).

encoding bluebell in iris might work for a semantics with only finite distributions, no concurrency, no while loops (just for-loops), adding state might already be hard

Now I see. I feel these are still far away. Getting finite distribution and finite loop right is already interesting for understanding and testing main ideas of bluebell. I still don't know which features matter more. The advantage of doing this kind of thing here is that we can easily find increasingly demanding examples.

I don't recall exactly and would defer to Julian or Frantisek who know a lot more about program logics than I do, but iirc that is taken into account by limiting ourselves to finite/countably infinite stuff.
Something in my mind is saying Peter Selinger and it has to be about while loops that do not terminate with non-zero probability.
I'm attending Italean today, so I need to skip today's meeting.
I have a couple of open PRs. One of these continues the replacement of the resource algebra https://github.com/Verified-zkEVM/iris-lean/pull/256 so that the resource algebra has a unit element.
Thanks! Sorry I missed these over the break.
